Win probability through a game

Source: R/games.R
win_probability.Rd

A Brownian-motion model of the score (Stern, 1994): the home margin drifts by mu points per game with standard deviation sigma, so with a lead m and a share r of regulation left, P(home wins) = \(\Phi((m + \mu r) / (\sigma \sqrt{r}))\). It needs only two numbers per league, both estimated from final margins by fit_win_probability(); defaults are the 2024/25 regular seasons. An expected margin per game (a betting line, or the difference in net ratings plus home court) can replace mu.

Usage

win_probability(pbp, params = NULL, expected = NULL)

fit_win_probability(pbp)

Arguments

pbp

Play-by-play in the ggbasket layout (see pbp), one or more games.

params

Output of fit_win_probability(): league, mu, sigma.

expected

Optional named vector of expected home margins, by game_id.

Value

The play-by-play with margin, time_left (share of regulation), wp (home win probability after the event) and wp_change.

Details

fit_win_probability() takes mu as the mean home margin at the end of regulation and chooses sigma by maximum likelihood on every in-game state (score, time left, final result), which calibrates the model to how often leads are actually lost. A floor of 15 seconds on the time left stands in for the possession that is still to come, so a three-point deficit with a second left is unlikely but not impossible.
